entry.title: Can Discrete Tokens Serve as Semantically Lossless Representations of Visual Signals?
entry.summary:
Discrete visual tokens represent vision in a discrete form analogous to language, offering a native interface for multimodal modeling under a shared next-token prediction objective. However, quantization error is widely assumed to cause unavoidable semantic loss, fundamentally limiting the semantic fidelity of discrete visual tokens and positioning continuous visual representations as an intrinsic upper bound. Using multimodal understanding as a proxy for semantic fidelity, we revisit this assumption and find quantization error unreliable, as discrete representations with substantially larger errors can achieve better understanding.

Source: Hugging Face Daily Papers · Tags: #llm #open-weights #inference

entry.title: HABIT-Bench: Evaluating Habit Induction from Longitudinal Weak Evidence in Agent Memory
entry.summary:
In long-term interactions with large language model (LLM) agents, users reveal habits through their choices and actions. These habits capture implicit user information that agents must infer across conversations. However, individual observations may provide only partial evidence about a habit or when it applies.

entry.title: ThinkWorld: World Imagination Reinforces Chain-of-Dynamics Reasoning
entry.summary:
Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have made substantial progress in robotic manipulation, but their generalization remains constrained by the diversity and coverage of action-labeled robot demonstrations. Human videos provide much broader behavioral and environmental experience, while learning from them faces a fundamental trade-off between scalable data and explicit action grounding. We introduce ThinkWorld, a VLA learning framework that grounds action reasoning in world dynamics and strengthens it through reinforcement learning with world imagination.

Source: Hugging Face Daily Papers · Tags: #llm #open-weights #robotics #reinforcement-learning

entry.title: Memory Tax: Dissecting the Net Value of Agent Memory
entry.summary:
Memory is increasingly used in long-horizon agents, yet the net value of building memory over direct retrieval from raw history remains largely unclear. Through a large-scale evaluation across multiple benchmarks and model backbones, we find many dedicated memory systems underperform naive RAG in many cases, indicating a negative net value. Taking RAG as a reference, we dissect the net value of memory into the gains and losses over direct retrieval, termed memory benefit and memory tax.

Source: Hugging Face Daily Papers · Tags: #llm #open-weights #agents #rag

entry.title: PDRVLA: A Vision-Language-Action Model with Physical Dynamics Representations
entry.summary:
Vision--Language--Action (VLA) models generate robot actions from visual observations and language instructions, but their understanding of physical dynamics remains limited. Video world models can capture scene dynamics, yet generating future videos introduces high latency into the control loop. We introduce PDRVLA, whose lightweight Physical Dynamics Module extracts physical tokens from vision--language features to condition action generation without online video generation.

Source: Hugging Face Daily Papers · Tags: #llm #open-weights #robotics

entry.title: Truncate or Not? A Scaling Study of Looped Transformers with Truncated Backpropagation
entry.summary:
Looped transformers reuse a shared block of layers to increase computational depth without increasing the number of trainable parameters. They are trained with backpropagation through time (BPTT). To save training compute, BPTT is often truncated to the last few loops, but truncation yields biased gradients that may weaken the benefit of looping.

Source: Hugging Face Daily Papers · Tags: #llm #open-weights

entry.title: The Trinity:Capability-Driven Recursive Self-Improvement for Multimodal Agents
entry.summary:
Multimodal intelligence can be viewed as human-guided co-evolution between worlds and agents through interaction. However, scaling this process faces two bottlenecks: constructing heterogeneous, verifiable environments is costly, and manual Harness iteration cannot keep pace with growing task diversity and complexity. A key insight is that tasks with different modalities and surface forms can share the same underlying capability requirements.

Source: Hugging Face Daily Papers · Tags: #llm #open-weights #agents

entry.title: Zooming without Zooming v2: From Seeing Details to Connecting Evidence for Generalizable Multimodal Perception
entry.summary:
Multimodal perception forms the foundation of multimodal intelligence. In particular, spatial perception and multimodal long-context understanding are two pivotal tasks that underpin embodied AI and multimodal agents. However, synthesizing targeted, high-quality training data for these tasks remains difficult and costly.

entry.title: Channel Selection for Mixture-of-Experts Decoding Needs No Calibration Data
entry.summary:
Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models are bottlenecked by loading routed-expert weights from memory during interactive decoding at small batch sizes. Because most intermediate channels in a routed expert contribute little to any single token, channel selectors predict which channels matter and read only their weights, typically keeping channels above a threshold calibrated on offline data. We show that channel selection needs no calibration data.

Source: Hugging Face Daily Papers · Tags: #llm #open-weights #inference
